analysis_kind: Exploratory model extension, not a new production policy or main-protocol change.
state: number of processed child commits since last validation
rule: Select if the frozen baseline selects OR age+1 >= K. A selected transition obtains finite-oracle truth and resets age=0; otherwise retain availability and increment age. Every transition counts, including unchanged source.
expected_bound: No reachable cycle of false availability; longest consecutive run of false-availability states is at most K-1, conditional on accurate completed validation.
projection: Lift each frozen hidden_missing transition using its target program and finite truth; force validation at the deadline. Check each resulting base state exists in the frozen graph.

negative_controls.rule: Incorrectly reset age to zero whenever source changes before evaluating the deadline.
negative_controls.expected: A reachable source-changing false-availability cycle violates the bound.

negative_controls.rule: Use age+1 > K instead of >= K.

workloads.truth: g=1 throughout; f calls g; unrelated VALUE toggles at every child.
g=2 from first child onward; f calls g; unrelated VALUE toggles at every child.
g=2 for children1..8, restored to1 at child9; f calls g; unrelated VALUE toggles at every child.

outputs: Full reachable lifted graphs and longest-run witnesses per K
Per-step workload decisions, ages, availability and logical validation counts
limits: Finite two-function grammar inherited from the frozen model; not arbitrary Python.
No Docker runs or runtime measurements; validation boundary uses known finite truth.
Periodic validation is a generic safeguard, not claimed as a novel idea.
Persistent false claims already withheld are rechecked at every transition by the original previously_unavailable rule.
No real provenance, labels, cohort, policy config or main protocol is changed.
